summary:
I wrote plan.md (nothing built or rendered). Soames-Dunn: a two-storey shop row facing west on Pike Place, with a taller range stepping up the bluff behind it. Brick piers, cream panels with paired windows, one long dark-oak awning; the brown Starbucks front, sign and round logo sit beside a blue Bavarian Meats board.
Butterworth: a long flat-roofed red-brick block, four storeys on 1st Avenue and six on its Pike Place back. Arched top two floors, a heavy sandstone cornice and a projecting entrance with a BUTTERWORTH name panel; the Kells pub front sits in the back basement.
It reads as the real north end because of the stepped slope, real names, brick-and-cream palette, flat parapet roofs and warm-lit shops; all blocks pass the 1.21.1 check. Two flat-roofed brick commercial blocks in site orientation: Soames-Dunn (two-storey west shop row with awning, Starbucks brown front and logo disc, Bavarian Meats, stepped B/E range up the bluff) and Butterworth (4-storey 1st Ave front with arches, sandstone cornice, BUTTERWORTH pavilion, Kells pub on the back).
Both are cut down to the ground map. Dusk comes from lit shopfronts, hanging lanterns and warm glow blocks behind two thirds of the upper windows.
elements.md and the plan.md PALETTE, VOCABULARY, ROOMS and PARTS sections are written. `chain` is the 1.21.1 id and the toolkit's check doesn't know it.
elements: Butterworth east front, pavilion, back and Kells (parts/butter-front.mjs)

summary: Soames-Dunn masonry shell: Soames-Dunn shell is built in parts/soames-shell.mjs. Masses A, B, C, D1/D2 and E have 2-thick brick walls footed to the ground map, stone_bricks plinths, dark_oak_planks floors and stucco upper fronts. Every opening in OPENINGS is carved as air. make.sh runs clean with no refused writes; I read one render and did not run `mcd check` or `mcd fit`.
polish: Not run: `mcd check`, `mcd fit`, and the P1 refused/off-palette line of the make.sh report. Only a render was read, and it showed the shell with the roofs still missing, as expected.
B north returns (z4 for x48..51, z8/z28) have no windows, because the plan lists none.
x2 y17 on the A front is left for the roof or cornice parts. Wall tops are deck-1, with the deck, parapet and cornice built by P3/P4.
Glow cells are left as interior air. Where ground is higher than a floor (A beyond x12, east E), the interior stays as buried dirt.
E has no lower floor under y11, so the lower storey is hollow behind its court windows (y7..9).

waste.what: Worked out by hand which face cells are exposed or interior, wall thickness, and per-face opening carving with ground clipping.
waste.cost: one ~110-line generator, no retries
waste.tool: A build-library helper `massWalls(g, masses, ground, {thickness})` plus `openings(g, faceSpecs)` that carves openings 2 deep and clips them to the ground map.

waste.what: Checked that the footprint, ground map and mass tables agree.
waste.cost: manual reasoning, no tool check
waste.tool: A `mcd footprint-check` that lists plan.md mass rects falling outside # cells.

companions.task: Quoins, string courses and sills on the B and E court faces
Fill the carved openings, with glass in the cell behind each plane

summary:
Butterworth masonry shell: parts/butter-shell.mjs builds the Butterworth masonry shell: 2-thick brick walls from ground to y35 on the plot 1 footprint, plinth courses, interior floor slabs over stone footings, and the pavilion walls.
Every opening (east shopfronts and windows, the pavilion doorway and windows, west back windows, Kells front, north/south end windows) is left as air in both wall layers. The red_nether_bricks back band sits at y35.
make.sh writes a whole build.nbt (Butterworth shell 66,907 placed, 0 refused, 0 off-palette); check is walkable and floating-free; render and zoom read as a red-brick mass with openings. plan.md P2 ticked and notes added.
polish: The east cornice zone x115 y34..41 and the east-face plinth/pilasters/sills/belt courses are left to P5, as planned. Nothing is built at x115.
The pavilion windows are cut through x116..117 (not x115): the glazier must put the glass in the pavilion's own layer. Noted in plan.md.
Floors show from above until the roof deck at y36 is built by P3; the interior is open sky there until then.
Arched F3/F4 windows are cut as rectangles (y26..29, y31..34). P5 builds the arch heads and keystones at x114.
Pavilion interior is a solid 2-wide wall (no room behind the doorway); the doorway leads to the air at x115 that P5 must leave clear.
The rear stub x88..91 z156..157 is not built, as specified.

waste.what: The footprint rows, the ground rows and every opening rule were transcribed by hand from the brief into code, and the shell is a set of per-face opening rules written out cell by cell.
waste.cost: About 10 minutes of authoring for roughly 67K placed blocks; the rules are easy to get wrong at the pier and bay offsets.
waste.tool: A build-library helper such as `shell_from_footprint(g, { fp, ground, top, thickness, openings })` that takes the footprint text rows and ground map (as in plan.md) and fills ring/interior walls, plinth and floors itself, so a part only states its opening lists per face (y ranges and z/x spans).

waste.what: Checking the pavilion and the wall openings by eye, one zoom at a time.
waste.cost: Three renders, about 1 minute.
waste.tool: A `mcd openings build.nbt --plan plan.md` report that lists every planned opening cell (from OPENINGS) that is solid, and every air cell in a wall that the plan does not list.

companions.task: Lay the wall courses between the openings and set the stone-brick plinth and quoins, so I'd only have to give the opening lists.
Hand over the wall with its openings open in both layers (x113 and x114 east, x64/x65 back) and the pavilion's glass cells at x116..117, so the glass goes exactly in the cell behind the shell.
Check the plinth and footing against the GROUND map on the bluff edge (west rows z4..51 and z84..107), where g is 1 to 2 and the walls step down to the ground.

summary:
Roofs and stacks: parts/roofs.mjs lays the flat decks (gray_concrete) and brick parapet rings on all six masses (Soames A/C y17, B/E y25, D1/D2 y10, Butterworth y36), with keep boxes for the facades and pavilion.
It also builds the eight brick_stack chimneys (solid, deepslate band, slab cap) and six vent_hutch units at the listed cells.
make.sh writes a whole build.nbt with no refused writes and no off-palette blocks; fit is OK; the Soames roofs pass check, and the zoomed Butterworth stack reads as brick with a cap.
polish: Butterworth deck (y36) and its chimneys and hutches float: check reports 8604 floating blocks, all of them in x64..113 z0..155. They sit on the Butterworth masonry shell, which is still a stub in this copy; they should settle once parts/butter-shell.mjs lands and make.sh is rerun.

Parapets and fronts are not finished: this part only lays the decks and the parapet rings; coping and pier heads on the street fronts belong to P4/P5 (the A/C street-front keep boxes at x0..2 and x4..6, y17..21, are left for them).
roof.json was not written, so runParts skips its roof step. That is intended: the roofs sit at four different heights, and roof.json takes one y. The roofs are laid in roofs.mjs instead.
Chimney stacks meet the decks with no flashing; the deck-to-stack joint is a plain butt joint, which is fine at this scale but worth a note for the finish pass.

The roofs are hand-laid, not from the roof tool: the tool's interior writes gray_concrete_slab, which is off the roof palette, so the decks are full gray_concrete blocks and the parapet rings are bricks with slab coping.

waste.what: Decomposed the masses (B and E with holes, the Butterworth main block) into inclusive rects by hand, and worked out each chimney's keep box and deck offset by hand.
waste.cost: about 15 minutes of coordinate arithmetic across 6 masses, 8 stacks and 6 hutches
waste.tool: A mask-to-rects helper that takes a plan's '#' table and the GROUND map and emits the mass rects (rectsFromMask already exists in roofs.mjs but is not exposed through runParts or plan.json).

waste.what: Tried the roof tool's flat-parapet style first; it fills the interior with gray_concrete_slab, which is off the roof palette, so I rewrote the deck and parapet loops by hand.
waste.cost: one failed make.sh run and a rewrite of about 40 lines
waste.tool: A roof option that fills the deck with the full block (not a bottom slab) and takes the palette's deck block, plus a roof.json form that accepts per-mass y and parapet so one roof.json can cover all six masses.

waste.what: Checked each chimney by zooming on it one at a time to confirm the band and cap.
waste.cost: several zoom calls, one per stack
waste.tool: mcd zoom with a list of --at points, or a contact sheet of all stacks in one render.

companions.task: Lay the coping slabs and the parapet tops on the street fronts and the Butterworth cornice line, so the coping joins the piers and pilasters cleanly.
Flash the joint where each chimney stack meets its deck, so the stack reads as sealed into the roof rather than set on it.

summary:
Soames front and shopfronts: Soames west front (parts/soames-front.mjs): piers, parapet, coping, pier heads, cornice, long awning with brackets and lanterns, window boxes, paired-window sills and lintels, Starbucks and Bavarian boards, the round logo, and A/C bay layout are placed; make.sh writes a whole build.nbt.
The shopfront bays (frames, bulkheads, doors, transoms, display glass) and the upper panes are REFUSED by runParts: soames-shell.mjs line 74 sets `air` on every opening, and runParts locks air in earlier parts' cells (1141 refused writes).
Needs an upstream fix: the shell must leave opening cells unset rather than `air`. Stucco panels and the B west string course also need a flush replace of shell brick, so they are left.
polish: Shopfront bays not built: posts, bulkheads, display glass, door pairs, brown transoms and head beams are refused because the shell carves the openings to air (soames-shell.mjs:74) and runParts locks them. Fix in the shell: leave opening cells unset, not `air`. Then rerun make.sh; the bay code needs no change.
Upper paired-window glass (x3, C x7) refused for the same reason; the sills and lintels are placed.
B west face (x28) windows: glass at x29 y20..22 refused by the same lock. The string course (smooth_sandstone at y24, flush on x28) is not built: it would replace shell brick.
Stucco panels (x2 y10..16, C x6) not built: they replace shell brick. Needs a front-part replace step or a shell that places stucco itself.
Bavarian Meats storefront and Starbucks timber/door/transom live in the refused bays, so the doors and glass in elements.md are not there yet (P6 owns the glass and door pairs).
Plinth stone_bricks under the piers was attempted but is air-only, so it may be partly skipped where the shell already footed the walls.

Elements.md ticks cover only what is built: round logo, name board, long awning, flower boxes, Soames cornice, parapets with coping and pier heads. The big display windows, upper paired windows and the Starbucks door stay unticked.

waste.what: Worked out the bay grid cell by cell by hand: pier z0..z0+1, display z0+2..z0+5, door z0+6..z0+7, post z0+8 for 11 A bays and 6 C bays, plus the B window positions.
waste.cost: about 15 minutes of reasoning and one rewrite of the module
waste.tool: A plan-to-coordinates generator, or a `bays(plane, z0, n, grid)` helper in vocab that returns the cell lists for each grid unit (pier, display, door, post, window) so a part does not restate the 9-block rhythm.

waste.what: Discovered the lock conflict only after a full make.sh run: my writes into shell-carved openings were refused, 1141 writes in all.
waste.cost: one full build and a read of parts-report.json
waste.tool: A preflight: runParts (or a `mcd check` step) should list cells that an earlier part set to air and that a later part wants, before the build, and the shell template should not write air for openings.

waste.what: Each air-only write was guessed. I added a local writer (`writer(g)`) that checks footprint and air before writing, but the vocab helpers (cornice_run, awning_run, shop_board) do their own air checks and never reach my counter.
waste.cost: some duplicated check logic; the skipped/placed counts are only partly right
waste.tool: A shared air-only writer with a counter (placed/skipped/refused) that all vocab helpers route through, so a part's report is complete.

waste.what: Checked the boards' banner colours by trial: off-palette `brown_wall_banner` and `blue_wall_banner` came from shop_board's default base colours and had to be swapped to black.
waste.cost: one extra make.sh run
waste.tool: palette.json should give the banner colours the shop board helpers use, or shop_board should take its colours from the palette.

waste.what: Read the render by zooming the west front by eye to confirm the piers, awning, boards and logo. There is no automated check that a shopfront bay has its glass and door.
waste.cost: two renders and a zoom
waste.tool: `mcd fit` or a glazing check that flags any opening in the plan with no glass or door.

companions.task: Fill the shop openings once the shell leaves them unset: display glass, transoms, upper panes and the B west glass, set into the wall with their connection states.
Build the shopfront timber per bay (stripped log mullions, planks head and bulkhead, door pairs with hinges) in spruce for Starbucks and dark oak for the rest.
Lay the plinth and the stucco panels (x2 upper, smooth_sandstone) and the B west string course, which all replace shell brick and need a flush-replace step.

summary:
Butterworth east front, pavilion, back and Kells: Butterworth east front (parts/butter-front.mjs): ground-storey piers, shopfront frames, F2 windows, F3/F4 arches, pilasters, main and pavilion cornices, pavilion parapet, tablet block and doorway, back sills, Kells frame via kells_front.
make.sh writes a whole build.nbt; this part places 3274 blocks with no off-palette blocks. Trim at x115 and the pavilion stand proud of the shell's x114 wall, and the shell is still a stub here, so refusals and floating cells are unknown until it merges.
Glass, doors, lettering and the Kells lanterns are left for P6, and no elements.md items are ticked because each built item is only partly done.
polish: Not verified against the real shell: butter-shell.mjs was a stub during this run, so runParts refusals and the floating F3 arch voussoirs (x114..115 y29..30) and orphan trim cannot be judged until the shell lands. Those floats should close once the shell fills the head row y29 outer cells.
The shopfront glass, the door pairs (centre of each shop, pavilion doorway via pavilion_door) and the transoms are P6's. Only the bulkhead, posts and head beams at x113/x114 y16 are mine.

The BUTTERWORTH tablet has its smooth_sandstone block at x117 y38..39 z140..151 but the black banner letters are P6's. The pavilion pilasters at x117 z140..141 and z150..151 are not built: the tablet took that column.

The Kells front came from kells_front (frame, fascia, door, lanterns) but its glass and spruce door are P6's, and the fascia letters too; the back sills at the wall plane are probably shell cells and will refuse.
The back band red_nether_bricks y35 and the back windows belong to the shell (P2); only sills are mine.
Plinth course is stone_bricks from ground to the shop floor at x114..115, but in a few cells the ground already reaches the floor, so the plinth is empty there. Not checked against the shell.

No elements.md or plan.md checklist items were ticked: the Butterworth four-storey item, the pavilion/tablet item, the Kells item and the cornice item are each only partly built here (cornice Butterworth half done, Soames half is P4's).

waste.what: Working out the belt, pier, span and window bay z-ranges by hand from plan.md (pier pairs 11..12, 23..24 ..., gaps 2..10, 13..22 ...; bays z6k+1..6k+3 skipping 23 and 25).
waste.cost: about 8 minutes of reasoning and one full rewrite of the coordinate list
waste.tool: a plan.md-to-JSON export of pier pairs, shopfront spans and bay windows per facade (the mcd plan command reads rooms, not facades).

waste.what: Discovering that vocab helpers mis-name ids: B.slab("brick") gives bricks_slab, B.log("stripped_dark_oak_log") gives a doubled _log id, and cornice_run's stairs= takes a stem, so smooth_sandstone_stairs got a second _stairs suffix (131 off-palette blocks on the first build).
waste.cost: one failed build, a helper rewrite, one sed attempt that failed on macOS sed -i, and an Edit fix
waste.tool: make the vocab helpers take full block ids (or validate with mcd blocks --check on each call) and document that stairs= and slab() take stems.

waste.what: Checking the trim against the shell by eye and by the check command, when the shell is still a stub, so every float and orphan is a false alarm for now.
waste.cost: one check run, reading about 20 lines of output, and no way to verify placement
waste.tool: mcd check with a --after-part mode that ignores cells of parts not yet built, or a shell stub that fills the wall plane so the trim can be judged.

waste.what: Writing a small slab() and log() helper locally, because the vocab gives no safe slab or log for brick and stripped logs.
waste.cost: two helpers, about 6 lines
waste.tool: a B.slab that takes a stem and appends _slab only once, and a B.log that takes the full id (stripped_dark_oak_log).

companions.task: Fill the ground-storey shopfront openings (x113/x114 between the frames) with glass panes, the centre door pairs at each shop, and the Kells glass and spruce door, and set the transoms over the doors.
Check the quoin pattern and the plinth courses on the pilasters and piers, and the cut_sandstone bases at floor+1 so the pier joints read as worked stone.
Letter BUTTERWORTH on the pavilion tablet (x117 y38..39) and the fascia names, using plaque/bannerWord with black banner letters facing east.

summary:
Glazing, signs, lights, sidewalk: parts/finish.mjs written and make.sh produces a whole build.nbt. It places the Starbucks and Bavarian Meats name boards, the lozenge, the BUTTERWORTH and KELLS letters, awning lanterns, shop and upper glow blocks, door-step slabs and the stone_bricks sidewalk.
The glass, shopfront doors and transoms (about 870 cells) are refused by the runParts lock because P1 writes air into the openings. Nothing is worked around; the fix belongs to P1 or runParts.
Not rendered or checked with $MCD fit; the only check run was $MCD check, which flags floating glass and unsupported banners that resolve once the stub parts are merged.
polish: 870 glazing writes refused by the runParts lock: P1 writes air into every opening, and the lock refuses later writes into air as well. Missing: Soames display glass (x2 y4..7), Soames door pairs and brown transoms, upper paired windows (A x2, C x6, B west x28), Butterworth shop glass and doors (x113), Butterworth arched and rectangular window glass (x113), pavilion glass and doorway (pavilion_door refused), Kells glass. The fix is for P1 to leave openings unwritten, or runParts to let a later part fill air an earlier part placed.

Shop-name and tablet letters depend on P4/P5 being built: the Starbucks board, the Bavarian board and the lozenge sit against the P4 front, and the BUTTERWORTH tablet against P5's parapet. None of them can be checked until those parts exist.
North and south end windows of Butterworth (x88..108) and the back windows (x64/x68) are not built; they face the z plane, so they need their own glass pass.
Starbucks logo bay: the upper windows of bay 4 are skipped as the plan says, but the round logo sits on P4 cells, so the logo is not checked here.
No render or $MCD fit run: the part was blocked by the lock, so the look at dusk is unverified.
Banner bases: only white, black and light_blue are in palette.json, so the boards use black and light_blue banner bases. Confirm the lettering colours read on the render.

waste.what: Found the air lock only after a full make.sh run: 870 glass and door writes refused, with no warning before building.
waste.cost: one full build plus the reading of parts-report.json, about 4 minutes of the 12
waste.tool: runParts should print the locked cells an earlier part placed as air, and a preflight step should list openings a later part must fill, before any part is written

waste.what: Writing each glass pane, door half and transom by hand with put() loops, with connection states set by hand.
waste.cost: about 300 g.set calls in my module
waste.tool: A glazing helper for a whole opening (glazing over a box with a pane preset, and doors by opening), so the pane connection states are set once

waste.what: Working out the Butterworth shop spans and floors from the pier list by hand.
waste.cost: about 20 z-values typed in
waste.tool: plan.md's bay table as data (pier and shop spans per face), read by the glazier code instead of retyped

companions.task: Leave the openings unwritten in the shell so the glazier's glass and doors can go in; this is the fix that unblocks about 870 cells.
Check the Starbucks and Bavarian board lettering and banner bases on the render, and set letter and base colours that read at dusk.
Place and check the dusk glow positions (shop ceilings, upper rooms, the chain lanterns under the awnings) once the glass is in.

summary: inspection: Fixed the 84 bottom-slab fit issues: full smooth_sandstone blocks under the F3 sills (y24) and under the pavilion tablet (y37 at x117). After ./make.sh the fit check reports OK and the walk is still ok with no unreached rooms.

waste.what: Located which module placed the floating sill. The fit line gave the cell (115,25,z) but not the helper, so I had to find that arch_window() in vocab writes the sill and that the belt course at y24 in butter-front.mjs is the bottom slab under it.
waste.cost: About 4 tool calls of grep and reading, plus one rebuild to see 84 drop to 12 and expose the second cause (x117 y38 tablet on the cornice cap at y37).
waste.tool: mcd fit should name the supporting cell and the part/helper that wrote it, e.g. 'supported by bottom slab at 115,24,z, written by butter-front belt course'.

waste.what: Worked out by hand that a top sill cannot be fixed by changing its own slab type: a top slab at y25 over a bottom slab at y24 still leaves air, so the support had to become a full block.
waste.cost: One reasoning pass and a rejected alternative (switching the sill to bottom or the belt to top), no extra builds.
waste.tool: The fit message could suggest concrete options such as 'make the supporting cell a full block'. The current advice 'make the slab a top slab or a full block' is misleading for a top slab sitting on a bottom slab.
